key_insight: An agentic, three-layer architecture uses LLMs to translate research questions into validated, reproducible scientific workflows, closing the semantic gap between scientist intent and workflow execution.
problem_solved: Scientists currently must manually convert natural-language research questions into workflow specifications, requiring both domain and infrastructure expertise; this paper automates that semantic translation so workflows can be generated reliably and reproducibly.
method: Semantic layer: an LLM parses natural-language research questions into structured intents and task plans.
Generator layer: validated code/generator modules convert intents into reproducible workflow specifications (e.g., DAGs, containerized tasks).
Execution layer: generated workflows are handed to scientific workflow systems for scheduling, fault tolerance, and resource management.
impact: Automates the most tedious, expertise-intensive step of experiment setup, speeding up iteration and improving reproducibility. Lowers the barrier for domain scientists to run complex, production-grade workflows without deep infrastructure knowledge.
visual_elements: A three-layer pipeline diagram (Semantic LLM → Generators → Workflow Engine) showing dataflow and responsibilities.
Before vs. After vignette: researcher text prompt on left and generated workflow DAG + execution monitor on right.
Example mapping: a short natural-language query mapped to structured intents and the resulting workflow spec (mini code snippet or DAG).
Icon set: LLM/brain, gear/workflow engine, checklist/shield for validation & reproducibility.
paper_title: From Research Question to Scientific Workflow: Leveraging Agentic AI for Science Automation
paper_authors: Bartosz Balis, Michal Orzechowski, Piotr Kica, Michal Dygas, Michal Kuszewski
